data.name: Netflix
data.notes:
###Why Traceroute Will Mislead You###

Connectivity to www.netflix.com is not indicative of connectivity to the Netflix content delivery service. Webpages on netflix.com are often served from AWS in the US and Ireland. The best method to investigate reachability is to expand the AS-NFLX IRR object and review those prefixes or alternatively contact our NOC email address for assistance.

###Peering in Brazil (PTT)###

A Netflix (ASN 2906) está no ATM do [IX.BR](http://ix.br) das cidades de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Porto Alegre e Fortaleza. Temos uma política aberta de peering, anunciando todas as nossas rotas para os route servers (ATM) desta localidades. Anunciamos um pequeno número de prefixos e não existe diferenças entre os prefixos anunciados para os servidores de rota (route servers) e sessões bi-laterais.

Se você é um novo membro no [IX.BR](http://ix.br), visite a [página de participantes](http://ix.br/particip/sp) e verifique os que possuem a designação de ATM. Isso significa que você já começa trocar tráfego com todos eles com uma única configuração com os route servers. A Netflix prefere as sessões de peering com os route servers do que estabelecer sessões bi-laterais para facilitar e agilizar as ativações. Também recomendamos que os participantes criem registros no [https://www.peeringdb.com](https://www.peeringdb.com) para fornecer visibilidade da suas redes e suas políticas de roteamento.

###MEDs###

We accept MEDs within a relevant geographical area (example: we will not serve UK content from Atlanta), but we automatically add a MED of 50 to PNI and 100 to IX in addition to the MED you send us. We use MEDs BEFORE geolocation - they will always override our geolocation service. Note that you will only receive prefixes relevant to the region that you interconnect.

### Geolocation and Proxy Blocking support ###
For support with geolocation and proxy blocking issues, open a request [here]( https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=43998445522957)

###AS40027 Assistance###

The email addresses in our AS2906 record cannot assist with connections from AS40027. For concerns with AS40027, please utilize our [partner portal](https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001068512-Getting-started-with-Partner-Portal#h_01G7T67328ABT7X95V6MPP626A) to connect with the right team.

###Additional Information###

Additional information about Open Connect, the Netflix CDN project, is available at [https://openconnect.netflix.com](https://openconnect.netflix.com)

data.name: Cloudflare
data.notes:
Cloudflare operates a global anycast network. All peers are required to have a complete PeeringDB entry and 24x7 NOC. PeeringDB is used for provisioning peering sessions. The number of prefixes we advertise will vary across sessions, and over time.

Automatic IX peering is available through [Cloudflare Peering Portal](https://peering.cloudflare.com). Authenticate using PeeringDB OIDC. ASN admins on PeeringDB are authorized to request peering.

Networks exchanging more than 10 Gbps of traffic in a single location may request a PNI. Only Nx100G LR4 connections are supported. Networks may also be eligible for embedded caches.

Peering and embedded cache guidelines available at [cloudflare.com/peering-policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/peering-policy/).

Submit verifiable abuse reports to [cloudflare.com/abuse](https://www.cloudflare.com/trust-hub/abuse-approach/). Do not send abuse reports to NOC / Policy email addresses.

data.name: Amazon.com
data.notes:
## AWS Peering - [https://peering.aws/](https://peering.aws/)

### Peering requests

#### IX
- Please use our peering portal to request IX peering sessions: [https://interconnect.amazon/](https://interconnect.amazon/) 

- *Note: If you're about to request IX peering sessions with AS16509 and currently do NOT have any peering with AS16509 established, please reach out to the regional contacts below.*

#### PNI
- AWS prefers 400GE, accepts 100GE and no longer supports 10GE PNIs.
When submitting a PNI peering request, please only address the specific regional contact listed below, related to the geographical region in which you wish to request PNI peering in.

- (Example: PNI peering requests for London should use peering-emea@amazon.com while PNI peering requests for Singapore should use peering-apac@amazon.com). 

- This will ensure your request is processed and addressed in a timely fashion. Please do not copy contacts not meant for peering policy in the location of your request.

#### ACE
- For ACE Embed cache information & operational issues please use our ACE portal: [https://interconnect.amazon/epop](https://interconnect.amazon/epop)

#### RPKI
- AWS drops all routes identified as RPKI invalid on incoming eBGP sessions.

#### Informational
- For details about our network, routing and interconnection options, please see [https://peering.aws](https://peering.aws). 

- AWS IP ranges with source location information: [https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json](https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json). 

- Please use the Maintenance alias only to notify us regarding maintenance activities on your end and do not copy other aliases into these inquiries. 

### Operational issues
- If you experience connectivity issues to Amazon AS16509, please reach out to our Technical Operations contact below. When contacting please include the following info to reduce the troubleshooting time: 
```
- Short description of the observed problem and impact 
- SRC & DST IP address 
- BGP peer information 
- Traceroute or similar valuable debug output. 
```
- Please **DO NOT** contact policy addresses for operational support.

- EC2 Reachability Test available at: [http://ec2-reachability.amazonaws.com](http://ec2-reachability.amazonaws.com)

data.name: BGP.Tools Route Collector
data.notes:
This is the route collector AS for bgp.tools. It does not carry traffic (apart from rare situations where it sends a single IPv6 prefix to a route server for backup reach-ability) on it's BGP sessions.

When peering with bgp.tools AS212232 you should export a full table (1M routes IPv4, 200k routes IPv6) like you would export to a potential customer. 

If you do not then bgp.tools will not be able to calculate your network statistics and the sessions may be removed to recover capacity. There are certain situations where internal resource shortages may mean not all prefixes are accepted/imported, but please export the full table regardless so this can be dynamically managed on our end!

data.name: V4LESS
data.notes:
# Policy / About

AS215250 is a testbed for evaluating running a network on RFC8950 / IPv4 Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) with an IPv6 Next Hop only.

The network is present at IXPs to allow network operators to experiment with interconnecting to a remote AS not using IPv4 for eBGP or internal transport.

In the future, sessions for all members on each IXP where AS215250 is present will be preconfigured in passive mode. Until then please reach out if you want to setup a session.

For peering sessions, IPv6 + Extended Nexthop is required. IPv4 sessions are not supported.

Please see the website for further information on how to run tests out of AS215250 (RIPE Atlas probes and NLNOG Ring nodes): https://measurement.network/services/v4less-as/
